page: Amazon Web Services m9g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 architecture running at 3.3 GHz. Operating with a 1:1 vCPU-to-core mapping without simultaneous multithreading, the hardware includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 96 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 768.0 GB of DDR5, establishing a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. The platform provisions a baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps, while including no local storage drives or discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations position the server in the top tier for multi-threaded computation and memory subsystem performance. The multi-core stress-ng score reached 382,009.03, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 107,871.7 and PassMark memory score of 4,353.81. Memory bandwidth testing shows 725.94 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 329.97 GB/sec for large-block writes. This high bandwidth yields 522.08 million Redis SET operations per second and 359.45 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-core stress-ng performance sits in the middle 50% tier at 2,010.28, and serial text generation on language models shows modest output due to lack of specialized matrix hardware.

The lack of hypervisor overhead on bare-metal hardware eliminates virtualization jitter, maximizing consistency for network and memory operations. Because no local NVMe storage is bundled, all persistence depends entirely on remote network storage over the 100 Gbps interface. Given its massive core count, high DDR5 throughput, and balanced resource footprint, this server offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads, such as distributed in-memory key-value databases, dense container orchestration platforms, high-throughput web serving tiers, and parallel data compression pipelines.
